title: Word: Copilot Chat edit mode creates and edits documents for users without a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence
summary: Hold: Microsoft Support documents an eligible subscription requirement and says Copilot opens in Word with Edit mode turned on, whereas the briefing reports these details as unstated. The roadmap facts and the Integrated Apps blocking path are accurate, but the licensing discussion also understates what Microsoft's comparison says about in-app access.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes conversational document creation, editing and refinement in Word from Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365): [Copilot Chat] Agent mode in Word enables conversational support to create, edit and refine document content from chat

claims.where: controls[1]; summary; Why it matters; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: No tenant UI or API switch specific to Edit mode alone is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Word" "Copilot" "Edit mode" "admin" "policy". Read Copilot settings, Manage Copilot Chat, TCM resources and Welcome to Copilot in Word; found broader controls, not an Edit-only tenant UI or API switch.

claims.claim: Block app is reached in Microsoft 365 admin center through Settings > Integrated Apps > Available Apps > app > Block app.
claims.quote: Select Settings, and then select Integrated Apps. ... Select the Available Apps list. ... Select an app from the Available Apps list to open the overview pane. ... Select Block app.

claims.claim: An API equivalent to the Integrated Apps block of the Copilot app is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Integrated Apps" "block" "Graph" API Copilot; "Copilot" "Integrated Apps" "PowerShell" block. Read Integrated Apps and copilotPackage:block; package blocking is not identified as the Copilot app switch.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Integrated Apps page restricts these controls to Global Administrators.
claims.quote: The following controls on the integrated apps portal in the Microsoft 365 Admin Center are only available to Global Admins.

claims.claim: Manage Copilot Chat describes Integrated Apps blocking as covering the Copilot app, Teams, Outlook and Copilot Chat on the web for all users.
claims.quote: This setting blocks Copilot in the Microsoft Copilot app, Teams, Outlook, and Copilot Chat on the web for all users.

claims.claim: The Integrated Apps page instead says app blocking covers only the Microsoft Copilot application and Outlook, while Teams honours Teams admin center settings.
claims.quote: The app is only be blocked in the Microsoft Copilot application and Outlook. Teams continues to honor the current setting for Teams Apps made in the Teams admin center

claims.claim: Learn does not explicitly say whether the Integrated Apps block removes chat inside Word.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph Integrated Apps block Copilot app API PowerShell app availability tenant block. Read Manage Copilot Chat, Integrated Apps and Copilot settings; none explicitly names Word as a host blocked by this switch.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Integrated Apps blocking is a tenant-level Copilot app control, not an Edit-mode-only restriction.
claims.quote: Blocking Copilot through Integrated Apps is a tenant-wide control that you can scope to specific users or groups, including licensed users.

claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365): [Copilot Chat] Agent mode in Word enables conversational support to create, edit and refine document content from chat

claims.claim: Prerequisites for Edit mode are not documented.
claims.quote: Copilot opens in the chat pane with Edit mode turned on. ... To use this feature, an eligible Microsoft 365 subscription and/or Microsoft Copilot license is required.
claims.fix: Replace the Prerequisites bullet with: '**Prerequisites:** Microsoft Support says an eligible Microsoft 365 subscription and/or Microsoft Copilot licence is required to use the Word chat-pane feature; availability depends on subscription, licence, organisation settings and platform.' Cite https://support.microsoft.com/office/welcome-to-copilot-in-word-2135e85f-a467-463b-b2f0-c51a46d625d1. Keep the roadmap's statement that this item serves users without the Copilot add-on.

claims.claim: The overview says Copilot Chat (Basic) users do not have access to Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint and OneNote.
claims.quote: You don't have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license and don't have access to Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.

claims.claim: The overview says Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) users can use Copilot in those apps without the add-on.

claims.claim: It is unstated which of Copilot Chat (Basic) and Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) carries the in-Word editing experience.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) refers to users without the Copilot add-on license, but who have access to Copilot capabilities inside apps (for example, Word or Excel). ... Word: Draft, rewrite, and summarize documents
claims.fix: Replace 'Which of those experiences carries Edit mode is not stated' with: 'The overview places in-app Word capabilities for users without the Copilot add-on under Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic); Copilot Chat (Basic) does not include in-app Word access.' Narrow the fourth Open question to: 'Does a feature-specific fair use limit apply to Edit mode?' Retain licensing.model as included and cite https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/copilot-overview.
